careerChapters.title: Physics & Research
careerChapters.summary: Graduate research and teaching in physics, including theoretical astrophysics, plasma physics, computational work, and undergraduate instruction.

careerChapters.title: Physics Project Management
careerChapters.summary: A short transition from academia into industry, leading physics courseware work before moving into defense engineering.

careerChapters.title: RF & Hardware
careerChapters.role: Principal Engineer, RF/Microwave Design → Hardware Engineering Manager
careerChapters.summary: A transition from hands-on RF and computational electromagnetics into technical leadership, phased-array development, internal R&D, and management of a 16-person CEM team.

careerChapters.title: Systems Engineering Leadership & Technical Execution
careerChapters.role: Systems Engineering Manager → Senior Staff Engineer, Systems / Lead Systems Engineer
careerChapters.summary: Boulder has remained my Northrop Grumman career base since September 2021. Here I led multidisciplinary ground-systems engineering and relay-station efforts and later returned to a senior technical lead role, without relocating my career base to Aurora.

ku-strong-hall.headline: Where physics became a profession
ku-strong-hall.summary: Lawrence was the center of my graduate research and teaching years at the University of Kansas and the starting point of my professional technical journey.
highlights: Completed graduate research in theoretical astrophysics and plasma physics.
Taught undergraduate physics laboratories as instructor of record.
Built the first-principles and computational foundation that continues to shape my engineering work.

charleston-sc.headline: The bridge from academia to industry
charleston-sc.summary: Charleston was a short but important transition chapter. I moved from academic physics into industry as a Physics Project Manager at Hawkes Learning before beginning my engineering career in Baltimore.
highlights: Led development of physics courseware for universities and colleges.
Applied technical depth in a product and project-management environment.
Spent approximately three months in Charleston before moving to Baltimore.

ng-bwi.headline: From RF design to engineering leadership
ng-bwi.summary: BWI was the first Northrop Grumman home base in my career. I started as a Principal Engineer in RF/Microwave Design and later moved into hardware engineering management.
highlights: Developed and maintained computational electromagnetics tools and modeling workflows.
Worked on active phased-array architecture, requirements, analysis, and performance modeling.
Led a 16-person computational electromagnetics team and an internal R&D portfolio.

ng-boulder.headline: Boulder: systems leadership and technical execution
ng-boulder.summary: The Boulder Gunbarrel District has remained my Northrop Grumman career base since September 2021, spanning systems engineering management, ground-system integration and my present Senior Staff Engineer / Lead Systems Engineer role.
highlights: Led systems engineering teams supporting operational ground-processing missions.
Served as SEIT lead for six next-generation relay ground stations on Guam.
Transitioned from engineering management into senior technical systems leadership while continuing to work from Boulder.
Connected architecture, interfaces, integration, verification and technical decision-making.

naval-base-guam.headline: Taking relay ground stations from design reviews to the field
naval-base-guam.summary: Guam became one of the defining geographic footprints of my systems engineering work. I supported the design, verification, build, and on-island execution of six next-generation relay ground stations.
highlights: SEIT lead through Critical Design Review for the six-site relay ground station effort.
Scrum Master from program startup through Preliminary Design Review.
Technical oversight of ground-terminal equipment and antenna subcontractors, including site visits.

camp-blaz.headline: On-island systems engineering
camp-blaz.summary: Camp Blaz was one of the Guam locations connected to my relay ground station work and on-site technical exchanges.
highlights: Field work tied to a six-site relay ground station program.
On-island coordination across government, industry, and subcontractor teams.
Part of a Guam mission footprint spanning northern and western installations.

andersen-afb.headline: Mission work on Guam's northern air base
andersen-afb.summary: Andersen AFB was part of the broader Guam mission footprint supporting my relay ground station systems engineering work.
highlights: Worked on-site as part of Guam program execution.
Supported technical coordination for ground infrastructure and mission interfaces.
Connected geographically to Camp Blaz and Naval Base Guam within the same program footprint.

raf-molesworth.headline: Professional work at RAF Molesworth
raf-molesworth.summary: RAF Molesworth expanded my professional map beyond the United States and Guam, adding on-site mission work in the United Kingdom.
highlights: Worked on-site at RAF Molesworth.
Part of a UK work footprint that also included nearby RAF Alconbury.
Molesworth and Alconbury are separated by only about eight miles.

raf-alconbury.headline: A second UK mission site
raf-alconbury.summary: RAF Alconbury sits only a short drive from RAF Molesworth and forms the second installation in my United Kingdom work footprint.
highlights: Worked on-site at RAF Alconbury.
Closely linked geographically with RAF Molesworth.
Part of the international expansion of my professional work map.

darpa-hq.headline: Work at DARPA Headquarters
darpa-hq.summary: Professional travel to DARPA Headquarters added a government R&D destination to the Mid-Atlantic portion of my career map.
highlights: Worked at DARPA Headquarters in Arlington, Virginia.
Distinct from Washington, DC professional travel on the map.
Part of a dense Mid-Atlantic work footprint centered on Baltimore, Annapolis, Arlington, and Washington.

westin-waltham-boston.headline: Phased-array systems and technology in Waltham
westin-waltham-boston.summary: I traveled to Waltham, Massachusetts for the 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Phased Array Systems and Technology.
highlights: IEEE International Symposium on Phased Array Systems and Technology.
The Westin Waltham Boston.

honolulu-hi.headline: A Pacific stop in Honolulu
honolulu-hi.summary: Honolulu extends the professional map into the central Pacific and gives the global view a natural bridge between the continental United States and Guam.
highlights: Professional travel to Honolulu, Hawaii.
Mapped separately from the Guam mission-site footprint.
The architecture is ready to expand farther into Alaska and Australia.

guam-general.headline: Two Guam trips. Two very different summit stories.
guam-general.summary: I traveled to Guam twice in support of RGS-A. The first visit was for an initial site survey, followed by an unexpectedly difficult hike to Mount Jumullong Manglo and an unforgettable stop at McKraut's. The second brought more Northrop Grumman colleagues, new things to learn, and a successful climb to Mount Lamlam. What I remember most about that visit is building friendships, trust, and memories with the team.
highlights: First trip: initial RGS-A site survey, followed by a wrong turn that led to Mount Jumullong Manglo instead of Mount Lamlam.
Lost the trail on the return, army-crawled through high grass before sunset, and found a gas station for hydrogen peroxide before discovering McKraut's, a lively German restaurant near the beach.
Second trip: traveled with a larger Northrop Grumman group, learned a lot, and successfully climbed Mount Lamlam.
Related Strava-backed hiking records: May 11, 2022 (Jumullong Manglo), and March 9, 2023 (Lamlam). These dates do not define the work-trip dates.
The second visit's most lasting impact was personal: Building friendships, trust, and memories.
